starting_points.name: Laravel installer with Livewire starter kit
starting_points.when: A new Laravel application using the official Livewire authentication/UI starting point.
steps: Select compatible PHP/Composer and Node/npm versions plus PostgreSQL and the PHP PostgreSQL PDO extension. Install the Laravel installer only if absent.
Inspect installed laravel new help; select Livewire and PostgreSQL explicitly. The example chooses Pest; use --phpunit instead if that is the project choice.

Configure ignored .env with the intended development database and secrets, review generated migrations, then migrate and build assets. Resume a failed installer database step from the generated project after correcting configuration; do not overwrite the project.

commands.cwd: A local source-workspace parent outside synchronized storage; my-app must not already exist
commands.purpose: Install the official installer only when it is not already available.

commands.cwd: A local source-workspace parent outside synchronized storage; my-app must not already exist
commands.purpose: Confirm flags supported by the installed installer.

commands.cwd: A local source-workspace parent outside synchronized storage; my-app must not already exist
commands.purpose: Generate the official Livewire starter with explicit PostgreSQL and test choices.

commands.cwd: The generated my-app directory after configuring its local .env and reviewing migrations
commands.purpose: Apply pending migrations to the intended development database.
Install starter frontend dependencies if the installer has not already done so.

notes: The installer may attempt database migration during creation; inspect its output and migrate:status before retrying. Database role/database provisioning and credential ownership must be established.

Omit --git/--github and decline repository-creation prompts: those optional modes commit files and GitHub mode can publish. --no-boost keeps optional agent integration separate; configure it afterward only if selected, honoring README/instruction-file policy.
Starter authentication is provided by Fortify. Resource policies, mail delivery and external identity choices remain application work; do not replace the starter auth by hand.

follow_up_generators.name: Eloquent model and migration
follow_up_generators.when: Adding an example Product domain resource.

commands.purpose: Generate an Eloquent model and companion migration.

notes: Replace Product with the actual domain; inspect php artisan help make:model. Add constraints, relationships, allowed assignments and tests before applying migrations.

follow_up_generators.name: Additive migration
follow_up_generators.when: The existing products table needs an example description field.

commands.purpose: Generate the next migration for an existing table.

notes: Edit the generated up/down methods deliberately and review SQL/data impact before php artisan migrate. Do not use migrate:fresh against retained data.

follow_up_generators.name: Livewire component/page
follow_up_generators.when: A new interactive server-driven page is required.

commands.cwd: The generated my-app directory with Livewire 4 installed
commands.purpose: Generate an example Livewire page component.

notes: Confirm installed Livewire version and php artisan help make:livewire. Current Livewire 4 defaults differ from v3 class-based paths; retain the starter convention or deliberately choose the supported --class option.

follow_up_generators.name: Authorization policy
follow_up_generators.when: The Product model needs explicit per-resource permissions.

commands.cwd: The generated my-app directory with Product model present
commands.purpose: Generate a conventional policy for application-specific authorization logic.

notes: Implement and invoke the policy, then test rejected requests; the generated stub does not establish access control.

preserve: Starter .gitignore, .env.example and secret exclusions, composer/package lockfiles, Artisan layout, Fortify auth flows, selected Pest/PHPUnit suite and Livewire/Tailwind/Flux integration.
Free versus paid Flux components remain a product decision. Preserve the working starter before customizing its UI or adding optional Boost/browser tooling.
verification: Run composer check-platform-reqs, php artisan about, php artisan migrate:status, php artisan test and npm run build.
Run the generated style/security checks available in the project; verify database tests use a dedicated test database.
Use composer run dev and verify registration/login and one authorized plus one rejected browser flow. Record resolved versions and generation choices.

sources.title: Laravel installer source: flags and optional commits

integration_steps: Configure ignored .env database/mail/queue settings for the features selected and confirm application key generation. Review the target database and migration status before applying pending migrations; preserve the starter authentication and selected test framework.
Build frontend assets and start composer run dev for local verification. Configure a supervised queue worker and scheduler separately for production when the application uses them.

If Laravel Boost is selected, add composer require laravel/boost --dev only if absent, inspect php artisan help boost:install and configure the chosen integration. Honor repository instruction ownership; for README-only policies inspect installer opt-outs or configure supported MCP integration manually.

When static analysis is selected, install a compatible Larastan development dependency and configure phpstan.neon from its installed-version guide. For selected browser testing, install laravel/dusk as a development dependency and run php artisan dusk:install; keep database/browser tests isolated.

For an authorized release, install locked production dependencies, build assets, review migrations, run php artisan optimize and reload supervised services. Confirm backup/restore and rollback compatibility before production migrations.
